text.tspan: Authors:
Christopher Hundhausen
I recently built a functional software prototype for an education research project in a few
hours. The same system would likely have required four to six months of development
from my research team in 2015, and we would have celebrated that timeline as efficient.
I'm not sharing this anecdote as a productivity flex but rather because it represents a
foundational shift our field hasn't fully reckoned with yet.
Insights

g.aria-owns: span4 span5 br5 span6 span7 br6 span8 span9

text.tspan: High-fidelity prototypes are no longer expensive to produce, breaking the
assumptions behind classic design wisdom.
Findings about low-fidelity prototypes eliciting more design feedback were
grounded in a world where polish signaled effort. That correlation has
broken.
The ability to effectively collaborate with GenAI tools to rapidly manifest
design concepts sits between traditional design and development roles.
